newsitem.title: USA: Boeing to settle antitrust charges - FTC.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to settle antitrust charges - FTC.

text.p: The Boeing Co will settle Federal Trade Commission charges that its $3.025 billion acquisition of Rockwell International Corp's aerospace and defense business would violate antitrust laws, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission said Thursday.

Under terms of the settlement, Boeing agreed to allow Allegheny Teledyne unit Teledyne Ryan, if it so chooses, to replace Rockwell as the wing supplier in a high-altitude endurance air vehicle known as Tier II Plus.
Under the pact, Teledyne Ryan would not incur any significant costs or risk in becoming the Tier II Plus wing supplier, the FTC said.
The agreement to settle the charges would also forbid Boeing from making any space launch vehicle manufacturer's non-public information available to its launch vehicle division.

The FTC had charged that the proposed acquisition of the Rockwell business would violate antitrust laws by reducing competition in two markets -- high-altitude endurance unmanned air vehicles and space launch vehicles.
